class LinearExpression:
    """
    A linear combination of function values, inner products (between points and/ or gradients)
    and constant scalars.

    Attributes:
    ----------
        ndim : int
            The dimension of underlying space, i.e., the size of each coefficient matrix.

        is_leaf : bool
            Indicates whether this expression is a primitive ("leaf") function value (i.e. not
            itself built from other `LinearExpression` objects). If `is_leaf` is True, this
            object is a function value defined from scratch.

        is_binary : bool
            Indicates whether a leaf expression is intended to be binary or not (i.e. constrained to only have values 0 or 1 in each dimension).

        decomposition_dict : dict
            A mapping from each leaf expression to its corresponding coefficient matrix. If
            `is_leaf` is True, this dict maps the object to its own coefficient matrix.

        counter : int
            Tracks the number of leaf `LinearExpression` objects.

    References
    ----------
        .. S. Diamond and S. Boyd. "CVXPY: A Python-Embedded Modeling Language for Convex
           Optimization." Journal of Machine Learning Research, 17(83):1-5, 2016.
        .. B. Goujaud, C. Moucer, F. Glineur, J. Hendrickx, A. Taylor, A. Dieuleveut (2022).
           "PEPit: computer-assisted worst-case analyses of first-order optimization methods
           in Python."

    """

    counter = 0
    # this is necessary else numpy will not even look at the @ operator due to precedence
    __array_priority__ = 1000
    # The Verifier a leaf is registered with; set by ``Verifier._register_var``.
    _verifier = None
    # ``(a, b)`` when this expression was built as ``a - b``; lets the Verifier
    # recognize a successive-residual objective (see ``Verifier.maximize``).
    _difference = None

    def __init__(self, decomposition_dict: dict, const: np.ndarray = None, is_binary: bool = False):
        """
        Initialize a `LinearExpression` object with decomposition dictionary.

        Parameters
        ----------
        decomposition_dict : dict
            A mapping from each leaf `LinearExpression` to its coefficient matrix (an nxn sparse
            matrix).

        const : ndarray or None, optional
            A one-dimensional array or None (default). If `const` is None, the `const` attribute
            of this object will be set to a `numpy.ndarray` of length `shape` filled with zeros.

        is_binary : bool, optional
            A flag to determine if a leaf element is intended to be binary (0 or 1 in each dimension) or not. Defaults to `False`.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If all the coefficient matrices in the `decomposition_dict` doesn't have the same number
            of rows.

        ValueError
            If `const` is not one-dimensional.

        ValueError
            If the number of rows in `const` does not equal the number of rows in coefficient
            matrices in the `decomposition_dict`.
        """

        for leaf, mat in decomposition_dict.items():
            if not isinstance(leaf, LinearExpression) or not leaf.is_leaf:
                raise ValueError("Decomposition keys must be leaf expressions.")
            if len(mat.shape) != 2 or mat.shape[1] != leaf.ndim:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Each coefficient must be a matrix with one column per leaf entry."
                )
        shapes = {mat.shape[0] for mat in decomposition_dict.values()}
        if len(shapes) > 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"All coefficient matrices must have the same number of rows: {shapes}"
            )
        self.ndim = next(iter(shapes), 0)
        if const is not None:
            const = np.asarray(const, dtype=float)
            if const.ndim != 1:
                raise ValueError("The constant must be a one-dimensional vector.")
            if not shapes:
                self.ndim = const.size
            if const.shape != (self.ndim,):
                raise ValueError("The constant must have one entry per coefficient row.")
        self.const = np.zeros(self.ndim) if const is None else const
        self.decomposition_dict = decomposition_dict
        self.counter = LinearExpression.counter
        LinearExpression.counter += 1
        self.is_leaf = False
        self.is_binary = is_binary
        self.branch_priority = 0
        self.lb = [i.lb for i in decomposition_dict.keys()]
        self.ub = [i.ub for i in decomposition_dict.keys()]

    @classmethod
    def from_int(
        cls,
        ndim: int,
        is_binary: bool = False,
        lb: float = -np.inf,
        ub: float = np.inf,
        branch_priority: int = 0,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        Initialize a `LinearExpression` object with an integer `shape`. Internally, this
        creates a decomposition dictionary that maps the `LinearExpression` object with a sparse
        identity matrix of shape `(shape, shape)`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ndim : int
            The dimension of underlying space, i.e., the size of each coefficient matrix.
        is_binary: bool
            Flag to determine if the leaf expression is binary or not (0 or 1 in each dimension).
        branch_priority: int, default 0
            Branching priority hint for a binary leaf: branch-and-bound solvers that
            support priorities branch on higher values first. Solvers without such
            a notion ignore it.

        Returns
        -------
        LinearExpression
            A new `LinearExpression` instance whose decomposition contains a single
            entry: the instance itself as a key, and a SciPy sparse identity matrix of
            shape `(shape, shape)` as the value.
        """
        _reject_nan_bounds(lb, ub)
        obj = cls.__new__(cls)  # uninitialized instance
        obj.is_leaf = True
        obj.decomposition_dict = {obj: spa.eye(ndim)}
        obj.ndim = ndim
        obj.counter = cls.counter
        obj.const = np.zeros(ndim)
        obj.is_binary = is_binary
        obj.branch_priority = branch_priority
        obj.lb = np.zeros(ndim) if is_binary else np.full(ndim, lb, dtype=float)
        obj.ub = np.ones(ndim) if is_binary else np.full(ndim, ub, dtype=float)
        cls.counter += 1
        return obj

    def __getstate__(self):
        # The Verifier back-reference is not part of the expression: copies and
        # pickles would otherwise drag in the whole Verifier and its solver models.
        state = self.__dict__.copy()
        state.pop("_verifier", None)
        return state

    def __str__(self):
        return f"Var{self.counter}"

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<LinearExpression {'Leaf' if self.is_leaf else ''}, dim={self.ndim}>"

    def __hash__(self):
        """
        Return a hash based on this expression's unique counter.

        Each LinearExpression is assigned a unique, monotonically increasing
        counter at construction. We use a tuple hash to avoid collisions with
        integers, which is necessary because __eq__ returns an EqualityConstraint
        (truthy) rather than a bool. Without this, dict[0] could incorrectly
        match a LinearExpression with counter=0.
        """
        return hash(("LinearExpression", self.counter))

    def __getitem__(self, item: Self | int):
        """
        Retrieve a coefficient matrix or a sliced LinearExpression corresponding
        to `item`.

        If the `item` is a leaf expression, this method returns its corresponding
        coefficient matrix. If the `item` is an `int` or a `slice`, this method
        returns a new `LinearExpression` instance representing a specified subset of
        rows from all the corresponding coefficients in the decomposition dictionary.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If the specified leaf expression is not found in this `LinearExpression` object.
        """
        try:
            return self.decomposition_dict[item]
        except KeyError:
            try:
                return LinearExpression(
                    decomposition_dict={
                        k: v.tocsr()[item] if spa.issparse(v) else np.atleast_2d(v[item])
                        for k, v in self.decomposition_dict.items()
                    },
                    const=np.atleast_1d(self.const[item]),
                )
            except TypeError:
                raise KeyError("""
                The specified leaf expression is not present in this LinearExpression object.
                """)

    def __add__(self, other: Union[Self, np.array, list, int, float]) -> Self:
        """
        Add two `LinearExpression` objects, ensuring they have the same dimension.

        Parameters
        ----------
        other : LinearExpression, np.array, list, int, float
            The expression or a vector to add to this one.

        Returns
        -------
        LinearExpression
            A new `LinearExpression` object whose decomposition maps each leaf in the union of both
            expressiom to the sum of its coefficient matrices, treating any leaf missing from one
            operand as having a zero coefficient matrix.

        Raises:
        ------
        ValueError
            If the objects (`LinearExpression` or a vector) to be added together does not have
            the same dimension.

        ValueError
            If the object to be added is not of one of the following types: `LinearExpression`,
            `np.ndarray`,  `float`, `int`, or `list`.
        """
        try:
            return LinearExpression(
                decomposition_dict=self.decomposition_dict,
                const=self.const + np.array(other).astype(float),
            )
        except ValueError:
            try:
                # Check to see if other is of type list or a numpy array
                if len(other) == self.ndim:
                    return LinearExpression(
                        decomposition_dict=self.decomposition_dict, const=self.const + other
                    )
                else:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Cannot add constant of mismatched dimensions. Expected dimension: {self.ndim}, got {len(other)}"
                    )
            except TypeError:
                try:
                    # Check to see if other is of type LinearExpression
                    if self.ndim == other.ndim:
                        merged_decomposition_dict = merge_dict(
                            self.decomposition_dict, other.decomposition_dict
                        )
                        return LinearExpression(
                            decomposition_dict=prune_dict(merged_decomposition_dict),
                            const=self.const + other.const,
                        )
                    else:
                        raise ValueError(
                            f"Cannot add LinearExpression objects of mismatched dimensions. Expected dimension: {self.ndim}, got {other.ndim}"
                        )
                except AttributeError:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Can only add LinearExpression objects to a LinearExpression object, numpy arrays, list, float, or an int got type {type(other)}."
                    )

    def __radd__(self, other: Union[Self, np.array, list]) -> Self:
        """
        Reflected addition to support other + expression.

        This method is invoked when a `LinearExpression` object appears on
        the right-hand side of a `+` operation (e.g. `np.array([1,2,3]) + expr`).
        It delegates to `__add__`, so that both `np.array([1,2,3]) + expr` and
        `expr + np.array([1,2,3])` behave identically.

        Parameters
        ----------
        other : LinearExpression, np.array, list
            The expression or a vector to add to this one.

        Returns
        -------
        LinearExpression
            A new `LinearExpression` object whose decomposition maps each leaf in the union of both
            expressiom to the sum of its coefficient matrices, treating any leaf missing from one
            operand as having a zero coefficient matrix.

        Raises:
        ------
        ValueError
            If the objects (`LinearExpression` or a vector) to be added together does not have
            the same dimension.

        ValueError
            If the object to be added is not of one of the following types: `LinearExpression`,
            `np.ndarray`, or `list`.
        """
        return self + other

    def __mul__(self, scalar: Union[float, int]) -> Self:
        """
        Multiply this `LinearExpression` object by a scalar.

        Parameters
        ----------
        scalar : float or int
            The numeric factor to multiply each coefficient matrix by.

        Returns
        -------
        LinearExpression
            A new `LinearExpression` object in which each leaf’s coefficient matrix is multiplied
            by the given `scalar`.

        Raises:
        ------
        TypeError
            If the `scalar` is not an instance of int or float.

        """
        factor = np.asarray(scalar)
        if factor.ndim != 0 or not np.issubdtype(factor.dtype, np.number):
            raise TypeError(
                "LinearExpression multiplication requires a scalar; use a matrix @ expression for vector scaling."
            )
        factor = float(factor)
        return LinearExpression(
            {leaf: coeff * factor for leaf, coeff in self.decomposition_dict.items()},
            const=self.const * factor,
        )

    def __rmul__(self, scalar: Union[float, int]) -> Self:
        """
        Reflected multiplication to support scalar * expression.

        This method is invoked when a `LinearExpression` object appears on the
        right-hand side of a `*` operation (e.g. `3 * expr`). It delegates to
        to `__mul__`, so that both `expr * 3` and `3  * expr` behave identically.

        Parameters
        ----------
        scalar : float or int
            The numeric factor to multiply each coefficient matrix by.

        Returns
        -------
        LinearExpression
            A new `LinearExpression` in which each leaf’s coefficient matrix is multiplied
            by the given `scalar`.

        Raises:
        ------
        TypeError
            If the `scalar` is not an instance of int or float.
        """
        return self * scalar

    def __truediv__(self, scalar: Union[float, int]) -> Self:
        """
        Divide this LinearExpression by a scalar factor.

        This method is invoked when the expression appears on the left-hand side
        of a true division (e.g. `expr / 3`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        scalar : float or int
            The numeric divisor to apply to every coefficient matrix.

        Returns
        -------
        LinearExpression
            A new `LinearExpression` in which each leaf's coefficient matrix is divided
            by the given `scalar`.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If the `scalar` is not an instance of int or float.

        ZeroDivisionError
            If `scalar` is zero.
        """
        if scalar == 0:
            raise ZeroDivisionError("Division of LinearExpression by zero is not allowed.")

        return self * (1 / scalar)

    def __neg__(self) -> Self:
        """
        Compute the negation of this LinearExpression.

        This method is invoked for unary negation (e.g., `-expr`). It returns a new
        expression with each coefficient matrix in the decomposition multiplied by -1.

        Returns
        -------
        LinearExpression
            A new `LinearExpression` object with all coefficient matrices negated.
        """
        return self * -1

    def __sub__(self, other: Self) -> Self:
        """
        Subtract one LinearExpression from another.

        Parameters
        ----------
        other : LinearExpression, np.array, list
            The expression or a vector xto subtract from this one.

        Returns
        -------
        LinearExpression
            A new `LinearExpression` object whose decomposition maps each leaf in the union of
            both expression to the difference of its coefficient matrices, treating any leaf
            missing from one operand as having a zero coefficient matrix.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the two `LinearExpression` instances have mismatched dimensions.

        ValueError
            If the object to be subtracted is not of one of the following types: `LinearExpression`,
            `np.ndarray`, or `list`.

        """
        result = self + (-other)
        if isinstance(other, LinearExpression):
            result._difference = (self, other)
        return result

    def __rsub__(self, other: Self) -> Self:
        """
        Reflected subtraction to support other - expression.

        This method is invoked when a `LinearExpression` object appears on
        the right-hand side of a `-` operation (e.g. `np.array([1,2,3]) - expr`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        other : LinearExpression, np.array, list
            The expression or a vector that this one is to be subtracted from.

        Returns
        -------
        LinearExpression
            A new `LinearExpression` object whose decomposition maps each leaf in the union of
            both expression to the difference of its coefficient matrices, treating any leaf
            missing from one operand as having a zero coefficient matrix.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the two `LinearExpression` instances have mismatched dimensions.

        ValueError
            If the object to be subtracted is not of one of the following types: `LinearExpression`,
            `np.ndarray`, or `list`.

        """
        return (-self) + other

    def __matmul__(self, other):
        # TODO
        raise NotImplementedError("np matrix or sp matrix should be on the left of the @")

    def __rmatmul__(self, matrix: Union[np.ndarray, spa.spmatrix]) -> Self:
        """
        Multiply this `LinearExpression` object by another matrix.

        This method is called when a `LinearExpression` appears on the right‐hand side
        of the `@` operator (e.g., `M @ expr`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        matrix : numpy.ndarray or scipy.sparse.spmatrix
            A matrix of shape `(m, n)`—where `n` is this expression’s dimension—to
            multiply on the left of each coefficient matrix.

        Returns
        -------
        LinearExpression
            A new `LinearExpression` object in which each leaf's coefficient matrix is
            multiplied by the given `matrix`.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If `other` is not a NumPy array or SciPy sparse matrix.
        ValueError
            If `other.shape[1]` does not match this expression’s dimension `n`.
        """

        if matrix.shape[1] != self.ndim:
            raise ValueError(
                f"""Matrix inner dimension ({matrix.shape[1]}) does not match
                    the LinearExpression dimension ({self.ndim})"""
            )

        try:
            return LinearExpression(
                decomposition_dict={k: matrix @ v for k, v in self.decomposition_dict.items()},
                const=np.asarray(matrix @ self.const).ravel(),
            )
        except TypeError:
            raise TypeError(
                f"""Expected numpy.ndarray or scipy.sparse matrix for multiplication;
                got {type(matrix).__name__}. """
            )

    def __le__(self, rhs: Union[Self, np.ndarray, list]) -> InequalityConstraint:
        """
        Build a less-than-or-equality (`<=`) constraint between this expression and
        another `LinearExpression` object or numpy vector.`

        Parameters
        ----------
        rhs: LinearExpression, np.array, list
            The right-hand side of the inequalit. Scalars are broadcast to the shape of
            `self`. Arrays or expressions must be of same shape with `self`.

        Returns
        -------
        InequalityConstraint
            A constraint object representing `self <= rhs`.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If `rhs` is not a LinearExpression object, NumPy array or a list.

        ValueError
            If the shapes of `self` and `rhs` are not compatible (i.e., not equal and
            not broadcastable).

        Notes
        -----
        This method does not evaluate the inequality; it only builds a constraint
        for the solver.
        """
        return InequalityConstraint(self, rhs)

    def __eq__(self, rhs: Union[Self, np.ndarray, list]) -> EqualityConstraint:
        """
        Build a equality (`==`) constraint between this expression and
        another `LinearExpression` object or numpy vector.`

        Parameters
        ----------
        rhs: LinearExpression, np.array, list
            The right-hand side of the inequalit. Scalars are broadcast to the shape of
            `self`. Arrays or expressions must be of same shape with `self`.

        Returns
        -------
        EqualityConstraint
            A constraint object representing `self == rhs`.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If `rhs` is not a LinearExpression object, NumPy array or a list.

        ValueError
            If the shapes of `self` and `rhs` are not compatible (i.e., not equal and
            not broadcastable).

        Notes
        -----
        This method does not evaluate the equality; it only builds a constraint
        for the solver.
        """
        return EqualityConstraint(self, rhs)

    def __ge__(self, rhs: Union[Self, np.ndarray, list]) -> InequalityConstraint:
        """
        Build a greater-than-or-equality (`>=`) constraint between this expression and
        another `LinearExpression` object or numpy vector.`

        Parameters
        ----------
        rhs: LinearExpression, np.array, list
            The right-hand side of the inequality. Scalars are broadcast to the shape of
            `self`. Arrays or expressions must be of same shape with `self`.

        Returns
        -------
        InequalityConstraint
            A constraint object representing `self >= rhs`.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If `rhs` is not a LinearExpression object, NumPy array or a list.

        ValueError
            If the shapes of `self` and `rhs` are not compatible (i.e., not equal and
            not broadcastable).

        Notes
        -----
        This method does not evaluate the inequality; it only builds a constraint
        for the solver.
        """
        return InequalityConstraint(-self, -rhs)

    def update_bounds(self, lb: np.ndarray, ub: np.ndarray) -> None:
        """Update lower and upper bounds of the `LinearExpression` objects."""
        _reject_nan_bounds(lb, ub)
        self.lb = np.maximum(self.lb, lb)
        self.ub = np.minimum(self.ub, ub)

    def bound_propagation(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Compute the elementwise lower and upper bounds of a linear expression
        given the bound constraints of its coefficient matrices.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
            A pair (lower, upper) representing the elementwise lower and upper
            bounds of the evaluated expression.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If any computed lower bound exceeds its corresponding upper bound.
        """

        def _interval_bound_propagation(
            a: np.matrix, lb: np.ndarray, ub: np.ndarray
        ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
            """
            Bounds the linear image y = A @ x for any x with lb ≤ x ≤ ub.

            Using midpoint m = (ub + lb)/2 and radius r = (ub - lb)/2:
                y_min = A @ m - |A| @ r
                y_max = A @ m + |A| @ r

            Returns (y_min, y_max).

            References
            ----------
                .. S. Gowal, K. Dvijotham, R. Stanforth, R. Bunel, C. Qin, J. Uesato, R. Arand-
                   jelovi´c, T. Mann, and Sigma. Kohli. "On the effectiveness of interval bound propa-
                   gation for training verifiably robust models. arXiv:1810.12715, 2018."
            """
            if np.all(np.isfinite(lb)) and np.all(np.isfinite(ub)):
                return (a @ (ub + lb) - np.abs(a) @ (ub - lb)) / 2, (
                    a @ (ub + lb) + np.abs(a) @ (ub - lb)
                ) / 2
            # An infinite bound (e.g. the unbounded output leaf of a linear
            # solve) makes the midpoint inf - inf = NaN, and the NaN then
            # spreads to every later bound. Split A into its positive and
            # negative parts and propagate the finite and infinite parts
            # separately, with the interval convention 0 * inf = 0.
            if spa.issparse(a):
                pos, neg = a.maximum(0), a.minimum(0)
            else:
                pos, neg = np.maximum(a, 0), np.minimum(a, 0)
            lb_f = np.where(np.isfinite(lb), lb, 0.0)
            ub_f = np.where(np.isfinite(ub), ub, 0.0)
            lo = pos @ lb_f + neg @ ub_f
            hi = pos @ ub_f + neg @ lb_f
            to_minus_inf = pos @ np.isneginf(lb).astype(float) - neg @ np.isposinf(ub).astype(float)
            to_plus_inf = pos @ np.isposinf(ub).astype(float) - neg @ np.isneginf(lb).astype(float)
            lo = np.where(np.asarray(to_minus_inf) > 0, -np.inf, lo)
            hi = np.where(np.asarray(to_plus_inf) > 0, np.inf, hi)
            return lo, hi

        out_lb, out_ub = np.zeros(self.ndim), np.zeros(self.ndim)
        for k, v in self.decomposition_dict.items():
            # Check the leaf bounds too: the infinite-bound path would read a NaN as 0.
            _reject_nan_bounds(k.lb, k.ub)
            _lb, _ub = _interval_bound_propagation(v, k.lb, k.ub)

            _reject_nan_bounds(_lb, _ub)
            if np.any(_lb > _ub):
                raise ValueError("Lower bound cannot exceed upper bound .")

            out_lb += _lb
            out_ub += _ub

        # Add constant term to bounds
        out_lb += self.const
        out_ub += self.const

        return out_lb, out_ub

    @property
    def value(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Value of the expression at the worst case found by the last ``solve``.

        For the MIP backend this is the solver's incumbent, a feasible point whose
        objective is a lower bound on the worst case returned by ``solve``.

        Raises
        ------
        RuntimeError
            If the expression is not registered with a ``Verifier``, no incumbent
            is available, or the expression has leaves added after the last solve.
        ValueError
            If the expression mixes leaves of different ``Verifier`` instances.
        NotImplementedError
            With ``method="sdp"`` or ``method="simulator"``, which have no incumbent.
        """
        if not self.decomposition_dict:
            return self.const.copy()
        # Leaves the canonicalizer creates internally (e.g. binaries) have no Verifier.
        verifiers = {
            id(leaf._verifier): leaf._verifier
            for leaf in self.decomposition_dict
            if leaf._verifier is not None
        }
        if not verifiers:
            raise RuntimeError("The expression is not registered with a Verifier.")
        if len(verifiers) > 1:
            raise ValueError("The expression mixes variables of different Verifier instances.")
        return next(iter(verifiers.values()))._solution_value(self)

def __add__(self, other: Union[Self, np.array, list, int, float]) -> Self:
    """
    Add two `LinearExpression` objects, ensuring they have the same dimension.

    Parameters
    ----------
    other : LinearExpression, np.array, list, int, float
        The expression or a vector to add to this one.

    Returns
    -------
    LinearExpression
        A new `LinearExpression` object whose decomposition maps each leaf in the union of both
        expressiom to the sum of its coefficient matrices, treating any leaf missing from one
        operand as having a zero coefficient matrix.

    Raises:
    ------
    ValueError
        If the objects (`LinearExpression` or a vector) to be added together does not have
        the same dimension.

    ValueError
        If the object to be added is not of one of the following types: `LinearExpression`,
        `np.ndarray`,  `float`, `int`, or `list`.
    """
    try:
        return LinearExpression(
            decomposition_dict=self.decomposition_dict,
            const=self.const + np.array(other).astype(float),
        )
    except ValueError:
        try:
            # Check to see if other is of type list or a numpy array
            if len(other) == self.ndim:
                return LinearExpression(
                    decomposition_dict=self.decomposition_dict, const=self.const + other
                )
            else:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Cannot add constant of mismatched dimensions. Expected dimension: {self.ndim}, got {len(other)}"
                )
        except TypeError:
            try:
                # Check to see if other is of type LinearExpression
                if self.ndim == other.ndim:
                    merged_decomposition_dict = merge_dict(
                        self.decomposition_dict, other.decomposition_dict
                    )
                    return LinearExpression(
                        decomposition_dict=prune_dict(merged_decomposition_dict),
                        const=self.const + other.const,
                    )
                else:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Cannot add LinearExpression objects of mismatched dimensions. Expected dimension: {self.ndim}, got {other.ndim}"
                    )
            except AttributeError:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Can only add LinearExpression objects to a LinearExpression object, numpy arrays, list, float, or an int got type {type(other)}."
                )

def __getitem__(self, item: Self | int):
    """
    Retrieve a coefficient matrix or a sliced LinearExpression corresponding
    to `item`.

    If the `item` is a leaf expression, this method returns its corresponding
    coefficient matrix. If the `item` is an `int` or a `slice`, this method
    returns a new `LinearExpression` instance representing a specified subset of
    rows from all the corresponding coefficients in the decomposition dictionary.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If the specified leaf expression is not found in this `LinearExpression` object.
    """
    try:
        return self.decomposition_dict[item]
    except KeyError:
        try:
            return LinearExpression(
                decomposition_dict={
                    k: v.tocsr()[item] if spa.issparse(v) else np.atleast_2d(v[item])
                    for k, v in self.decomposition_dict.items()
                },
                const=np.atleast_1d(self.const[item]),
            )
        except TypeError:
            raise KeyError("""
            The specified leaf expression is not present in this LinearExpression object.
            """)

def __hash__(self):
    """
    Return a hash based on this expression's unique counter.

    Each LinearExpression is assigned a unique, monotonically increasing
    counter at construction. We use a tuple hash to avoid collisions with
    integers, which is necessary because __eq__ returns an EqualityConstraint
    (truthy) rather than a bool. Without this, dict[0] could incorrectly
    match a LinearExpression with counter=0.
    """
    return hash(("LinearExpression", self.counter))

def __init__(self, decomposition_dict: dict, const: np.ndarray = None, is_binary: bool = False):
    """
    Initialize a `LinearExpression` object with decomposition dictionary.

    Parameters
    ----------
    decomposition_dict : dict
        A mapping from each leaf `LinearExpression` to its coefficient matrix (an nxn sparse
        matrix).

    const : ndarray or None, optional
        A one-dimensional array or None (default). If `const` is None, the `const` attribute
        of this object will be set to a `numpy.ndarray` of length `shape` filled with zeros.

    is_binary : bool, optional
        A flag to determine if a leaf element is intended to be binary (0 or 1 in each dimension) or not. Defaults to `False`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If all the coefficient matrices in the `decomposition_dict` doesn't have the same number
        of rows.

    ValueError
        If `const` is not one-dimensional.

    ValueError
        If the number of rows in `const` does not equal the number of rows in coefficient
        matrices in the `decomposition_dict`.
    """

    for leaf, mat in decomposition_dict.items():
        if not isinstance(leaf, LinearExpression) or not leaf.is_leaf:
            raise ValueError("Decomposition keys must be leaf expressions.")
        if len(mat.shape) != 2 or mat.shape[1] != leaf.ndim:
            raise ValueError(
                "Each coefficient must be a matrix with one column per leaf entry."
            )
    shapes = {mat.shape[0] for mat in decomposition_dict.values()}
    if len(shapes) > 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"All coefficient matrices must have the same number of rows: {shapes}"
        )
    self.ndim = next(iter(shapes), 0)
    if const is not None:
        const = np.asarray(const, dtype=float)
        if const.ndim != 1:
            raise ValueError("The constant must be a one-dimensional vector.")
        if not shapes:
            self.ndim = const.size
        if const.shape != (self.ndim,):
            raise ValueError("The constant must have one entry per coefficient row.")
    self.const = np.zeros(self.ndim) if const is None else const
    self.decomposition_dict = decomposition_dict
    self.counter = LinearExpression.counter
    LinearExpression.counter += 1
    self.is_leaf = False
    self.is_binary = is_binary
    self.branch_priority = 0
    self.lb = [i.lb for i in decomposition_dict.keys()]
    self.ub = [i.ub for i in decomposition_dict.keys()]

def __mul__(self, scalar: Union[float, int]) -> Self:
    """
    Multiply this `LinearExpression` object by a scalar.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scalar : float or int
        The numeric factor to multiply each coefficient matrix by.

    Returns
    -------
    LinearExpression
        A new `LinearExpression` object in which each leaf’s coefficient matrix is multiplied
        by the given `scalar`.

    Raises:
    ------
    TypeError
        If the `scalar` is not an instance of int or float.

    """
    factor = np.asarray(scalar)
    if factor.ndim != 0 or not np.issubdtype(factor.dtype, np.number):
        raise TypeError(
            "LinearExpression multiplication requires a scalar; use a matrix @ expression for vector scaling."
        )
    factor = float(factor)
    return LinearExpression(
        {leaf: coeff * factor for leaf, coeff in self.decomposition_dict.items()},
        const=self.const * factor,
    )

def __rmatmul__(self, matrix: Union[np.ndarray, spa.spmatrix]) -> Self:
    """
    Multiply this `LinearExpression` object by another matrix.

    This method is called when a `LinearExpression` appears on the right‐hand side
    of the `@` operator (e.g., `M @ expr`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    matrix : numpy.ndarray or scipy.sparse.spmatrix
        A matrix of shape `(m, n)`—where `n` is this expression’s dimension—to
        multiply on the left of each coefficient matrix.

    Returns
    -------
    LinearExpression
        A new `LinearExpression` object in which each leaf's coefficient matrix is
        multiplied by the given `matrix`.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If `other` is not a NumPy array or SciPy sparse matrix.
    ValueError
        If `other.shape[1]` does not match this expression’s dimension `n`.
    """

    if matrix.shape[1] != self.ndim:
        raise ValueError(
            f"""Matrix inner dimension ({matrix.shape[1]}) does not match
                the LinearExpression dimension ({self.ndim})"""
        )

    try:
        return LinearExpression(
            decomposition_dict={k: matrix @ v for k, v in self.decomposition_dict.items()},
            const=np.asarray(matrix @ self.const).ravel(),
        )
    except TypeError:
        raise TypeError(
            f"""Expected numpy.ndarray or scipy.sparse matrix for multiplication;
            got {type(matrix).__name__}. """
        )

def __sub__(self, other: Self) -> Self:
    """
    Subtract one LinearExpression from another.

    Parameters
    ----------
    other : LinearExpression, np.array, list
        The expression or a vector xto subtract from this one.

    Returns
    -------
    LinearExpression
        A new `LinearExpression` object whose decomposition maps each leaf in the union of
        both expression to the difference of its coefficient matrices, treating any leaf
        missing from one operand as having a zero coefficient matrix.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the two `LinearExpression` instances have mismatched dimensions.

    ValueError
        If the object to be subtracted is not of one of the following types: `LinearExpression`,
        `np.ndarray`, or `list`.

    """
    result = self + (-other)
    if isinstance(other, LinearExpression):
        result._difference = (self, other)
    return result

def __truediv__(self, scalar: Union[float, int]) -> Self:
    """
    Divide this LinearExpression by a scalar factor.

    This method is invoked when the expression appears on the left-hand side
    of a true division (e.g. `expr / 3`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    scalar : float or int
        The numeric divisor to apply to every coefficient matrix.

    -------

        A new `LinearExpression` in which each leaf's coefficient matrix is divided
        by the given `scalar`.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If the `scalar` is not an instance of int or float.

    ZeroDivisionError
        If `scalar` is zero.

    if scalar == 0:
        raise ZeroDivisionError("Division of LinearExpression by zero is not allowed.")

def bound_propagation(self) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Compute the elementwise lower and upper bounds of a linear expression
    given the bound constraints of its coefficient matrices.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
        A pair (lower, upper) representing the elementwise lower and upper
        bounds of the evaluated expression.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If any computed lower bound exceeds its corresponding upper bound.
    """

    def _interval_bound_propagation(
        a: np.matrix, lb: np.ndarray, ub: np.ndarray
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Bounds the linear image y = A @ x for any x with lb ≤ x ≤ ub.

        Using midpoint m = (ub + lb)/2 and radius r = (ub - lb)/2:
            y_min = A @ m - |A| @ r
            y_max = A @ m + |A| @ r

        Returns (y_min, y_max).

        References
        ----------
            .. S. Gowal, K. Dvijotham, R. Stanforth, R. Bunel, C. Qin, J. Uesato, R. Arand-
               jelovi´c, T. Mann, and Sigma. Kohli. "On the effectiveness of interval bound propa-
               gation for training verifiably robust models. arXiv:1810.12715, 2018."
        """
        if np.all(np.isfinite(lb)) and np.all(np.isfinite(ub)):
            return (a @ (ub + lb) - np.abs(a) @ (ub - lb)) / 2, (
                a @ (ub + lb) + np.abs(a) @ (ub - lb)
            ) / 2
        # An infinite bound (e.g. the unbounded output leaf of a linear
        # solve) makes the midpoint inf - inf = NaN, and the NaN then
        # spreads to every later bound. Split A into its positive and
        # negative parts and propagate the finite and infinite parts
        # separately, with the interval convention 0 * inf = 0.
        if spa.issparse(a):
            pos, neg = a.maximum(0), a.minimum(0)
        else:
            pos, neg = np.maximum(a, 0), np.minimum(a, 0)
        lb_f = np.where(np.isfinite(lb), lb, 0.0)
        ub_f = np.where(np.isfinite(ub), ub, 0.0)
        lo = pos @ lb_f + neg @ ub_f
        hi = pos @ ub_f + neg @ lb_f
        to_minus_inf = pos @ np.isneginf(lb).astype(float) - neg @ np.isposinf(ub).astype(float)
        to_plus_inf = pos @ np.isposinf(ub).astype(float) - neg @ np.isneginf(lb).astype(float)
        lo = np.where(np.asarray(to_minus_inf) > 0, -np.inf, lo)
        hi = np.where(np.asarray(to_plus_inf) > 0, np.inf, hi)
        return lo, hi

    out_lb, out_ub = np.zeros(self.ndim), np.zeros(self.ndim)
    for k, v in self.decomposition_dict.items():
        # Check the leaf bounds too: the infinite-bound path would read a NaN as 0.
        _reject_nan_bounds(k.lb, k.ub)
        _lb, _ub = _interval_bound_propagation(v, k.lb, k.ub)

        _reject_nan_bounds(_lb, _ub)
        if np.any(_lb > _ub):
            raise ValueError("Lower bound cannot exceed upper bound .")

        out_lb += _lb
        out_ub += _ub

    # Add constant term to bounds
    out_lb += self.const
    out_ub += self.const

    return out_lb, out_ub

@classmethod
def from_int(
    cls,
    ndim: int,
    is_binary: bool = False,
    lb: float = -np.inf,
    ub: float = np.inf,
    branch_priority: int = 0,
) -> Self:
    """
    Initialize a `LinearExpression` object with an integer `shape`. Internally, this
    creates a decomposition dictionary that maps the `LinearExpression` object with a sparse
    identity matrix of shape `(shape, shape)`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ndim : int
        The dimension of underlying space, i.e., the size of each coefficient matrix.
    is_binary: bool
        Flag to determine if the leaf expression is binary or not (0 or 1 in each dimension).
    branch_priority: int, default 0
        Branching priority hint for a binary leaf: branch-and-bound solvers that
        support priorities branch on higher values first. Solvers without such
        a notion ignore it.

    Returns
    -------
    LinearExpression
        A new `LinearExpression` instance whose decomposition contains a single
        entry: the instance itself as a key, and a SciPy sparse identity matrix of
        shape `(shape, shape)` as the value.
    """
    _reject_nan_bounds(lb, ub)
    obj = cls.__new__(cls)  # uninitialized instance
    obj.is_leaf = True
    obj.decomposition_dict = {obj: spa.eye(ndim)}
    obj.ndim = ndim
    obj.counter = cls.counter
    obj.const = np.zeros(ndim)
    obj.is_binary = is_binary
    obj.branch_priority = branch_priority
    obj.lb = np.zeros(ndim) if is_binary else np.full(ndim, lb, dtype=float)
    obj.ub = np.ones(ndim) if is_binary else np.full(ndim, ub, dtype=float)
    cls.counter += 1
    return obj

def update_bounds(self, lb: np.ndarray, ub: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Update lower and upper bounds of the `LinearExpression` objects."""

    self.lb = np.maximum(self.lb, lb)
    self.ub = np.minimum(self.ub, ub)

docs.title: Proxable functions
docs.text: Proxable functions are convex functions whose proximal operators can be used as steps, each supplying a numerical prox and the encoding needed by the verification problem. Use vp.prox(function, arg, gamma=1.0); support varies by backend, and unsupported operations raise explicitly. They all derive from the abstract base class below.

docs.title: ProxableFunction
docs.text:
Abstract base class for proxable functions.

A function \(f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{+\infty\}\) is proxable if its proximal operator

\[ \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x) = \arg\!\min_{u} \left\{ f(u) + \frac{1}{2\gamma} \|u - x\|^2 \right\} \]

can be evaluated efficiently (in closed form or via a structured subproblem).

Subclasses provide the numerical interface (eval, prox, grad). The mapping from a proxable function to one or more steps lives in the step decomposer's _PROX_DECOMPOSERS registry — it is not a method on this class.

Source code in fomtools/proxable_functions/proximal_operator.py 
class ProxableFunction:
    r"""
    Abstract base class for proxable functions.

    A function $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{+\infty\}$ is proxable
    if its proximal operator

    $$
        \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x) = \arg\!\min_{u} \left\{ f(u)
        + \frac{1}{2\gamma} \|u - x\|^2 \right\}
    $$

    can be evaluated efficiently (in closed form or via a structured subproblem).

    Subclasses provide the numerical interface (``eval``, ``prox``, ``grad``).
    The mapping from a proxable function to one or more steps lives in the
    step decomposer's ``_PROX_DECOMPOSERS`` registry — it is *not* a method
    on this class.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        pass

    def eval(self, x: np.ndarray) -> float:
        r"""
        Evaluate $f(x)$.

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the function.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            The function value $f(x)$.

        Raises
        ------
        NotImplementedError
            Raised by the base class; must be implemented by subclasses.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def prox(self, arg: np.ndarray, gamma: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Compute the proximal point of the function.

        Solves

        $$
            \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg}) = \arg\!\min_{u} \left\{
            f(u) + \frac{1}{2\gamma} \|u - \text{arg}\|^2 \right\}.
        $$

        Parameters
        ----------
        arg : np.ndarray
            Input point at which to evaluate the proximal operator.
        gamma : float, default 1.0
            Step size $\gamma > 0$.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            The proximal point $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.

        Raises
        ------
        NotImplementedError
            Raised by the base class; must be implemented by subclasses.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def grad(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Compute the gradient (or a subgradient) of the function at ``x``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the (sub)gradient.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            Gradient $\nabla f(x)$ or a subgradient when $f$ is non-smooth.

        Raises
        ------
        NotImplementedError
            Raised by the base class; must be implemented by subclasses.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

docs.text:
Bases: ProxableFunction

Elastic-net regularizer.

Represents

\[ f(x) = \alpha \|x\|_1 + \beta \|x\|_2^2. \]

Convex; strongly convex when \(\beta > 0\). Note that the \(\ell_2\) term has no leading \(1/2\) factor: \(\nabla(\beta \|x\|_2^2) = 2\beta x\).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default alpha float

Weight \(\alpha \ge 0\) of the \(\ell_1\) term.

required beta float

Weight \(\beta \ge 0\) of the squared \(\ell_2\) term.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If alpha or beta is negative.

See Also

NormL1 : The case \(\beta = 0\), identical to NormL1(lambd=alpha).

Notes

Proximal operator.

\[ \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) = \frac{S_{\alpha\gamma}(v)}{1 + 2\beta\gamma}, \]

where \(S_\lambda(w) = \operatorname{sign}(w)\,\max(|w| - \lambda, 0)\) is element-wise soft thresholding. For \(\alpha = 0\) it reduces to the ridge shrinkage \(v / (1 + 2\beta\gamma)\).

Verification lowering. prox_elasticnet posts a single SoftThreshold step with threshold \(\alpha\gamma\) and scales its output by \(1 / (1 + 2\beta\gamma)\).

    r"""
    Elastic-net regularizer.

    Represents

    $$
        f(x) = \alpha \|x\|_1 + \beta \|x\|_2^2.
    $$

    Convex; strongly convex when $\beta > 0$. Note that the $\ell_2$ term has
    no leading $1/2$ factor: $\nabla(\beta \|x\|_2^2) = 2\beta x$.

    $$
        \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) =
            \frac{S_{\alpha\gamma}(v)}{1 + 2\beta\gamma},
    $$

    where $S_\lambda(w) = \operatorname{sign}(w)\,\max(|w| - \lambda, 0)$ is
    element-wise soft thresholding. For $\alpha = 0$ it reduces to the ridge
    shrinkage $v / (1 + 2\beta\gamma)$.

    **Verification lowering.** ``prox_elasticnet`` posts a single
    ``SoftThreshold`` step with threshold $\alpha\gamma$ and scales its output
    by $1 / (1 + 2\beta\gamma)$.
    """

    def __init__(self, alpha: float, beta: float):
        super().__init__()
        if alpha < 0 or beta < 0:
            raise ValueError("alpha and beta must be non-negative")
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.beta = beta

    def eval(self, x: np.ndarray) -> float:
        r"""
        Evaluate $f(x) = \alpha\|x\|_1 + \beta\|x\|_2^2$.

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the function.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            The function value $f(x)$.
        """
        return float(self.alpha * np.sum(np.abs(x)) + self.beta * np.sum(x * x))

    def prox(self, arg: np.ndarray, gamma: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Compute $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.

        Uses the closed form

        $$
            \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg}) =
                \frac{S_{\alpha\gamma}(\text{arg})}{1 + 2\beta\gamma}.
        $$

        Parameters
        ----------
        arg : np.ndarray
            Input point.
        gamma : float, default 1.0
            Step size $\gamma > 0$.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            The proximal point $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.
        """
        thresh = self.alpha * gamma
        soft = np.sign(arg) * np.maximum(np.abs(arg) - thresh, 0.0)
        return soft / (1.0 + 2.0 * self.beta * gamma)

    def grad(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Compute a subgradient of $f$ at ``x``.

        Per coordinate,

        $$
            g_i = 2\beta x_i + \alpha \begin{cases}
                1   & x_i > 0 \\
                0   & x_i = 0 \\
                -1  & x_i < 0,
            \end{cases}
        $$

        where $0 \in [-1, 1]$ is the canonical choice at the kink $x_i = 0$.

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the subgradient.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            A subgradient $g \in \partial f(x)$.
        """
        return 2.0 * self.beta * x + self.alpha * np.sign(x)

Notes

\[ \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) = \begin{cases} v + \gamma & v < 1 - \gamma \\ 1 & 1 - \gamma \le v \le 1 \\ v & v > 1, \end{cases} \]

which collapses to \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) = v + \mathrm{satlin}(1 - v;\, 0,\, \gamma)\).

class HingeLoss(ProxableFunction):
    r"""
    Hinge loss (unlabeled).

    Represents

    $$
        f(x) = \sum_i \max(0, 1 - x_i).
    $$

    Convex and piecewise linear.

    See Also
    --------
    LabeledHingeLoss : Labeled variant $\sum_i \max(0, 1 - y_i x_i)$.

    Notes
    -----
    **Proximal operator.** Element-wise separable; per coordinate,

    $$
        \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) = \begin{cases}
            v + \gamma & v < 1 - \gamma \\
            1          & 1 - \gamma \le v \le 1 \\
            v          & v > 1,
        \end{cases}
    $$

    which collapses to
    $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) = v + \mathrm{satlin}(1 - v;\, 0,\, \gamma)$.

    **Verification lowering.** ``prox_hingeloss`` posts a single
    ``SaturatedLinear`` clip of the margin residual $1 - v$ to $[0, \gamma]$
    and adds it back to the input.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

    def eval(self, x: np.ndarray) -> float:
        r"""
        Evaluate $f(x) = \sum_i \max(0, 1 - x_i)$.

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the function.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            The function value $f(x)$.
        """
        return float(np.sum(np.maximum(0.0, 1.0 - x)))

    def prox(self, arg: np.ndarray, gamma: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Compute $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.

        Uses the closed form

        $$
            \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})
            = \text{arg} + \mathrm{satlin}(1 - \text{arg};\, 0,\, \gamma).
        $$

        Parameters
        ----------
        arg : np.ndarray
            Input point.
        gamma : float, default 1.0
            Step size $\gamma > 0$.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            The proximal point $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.
        """
        return arg + np.minimum(np.maximum(1.0 - arg, 0.0), gamma)

    def grad(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Compute a subgradient of $f$ at ``x``.

        Per coordinate,

        $$
            g_i = \begin{cases}
                -1  & x_i < 1 \\
                0   & x_i \geq 1,
            \end{cases}
        $$

        where $0 \in [-1, 0]$ is the canonical choice at the kink $x_i = 1$.

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the subgradient.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            A subgradient $g \in \partial f(x)$.
        """
        return -(x < 1).astype(float)

docs.text:
Bases: ProxableFunction

Element-wise Huber loss.

Represents

\[ f(x) = \sum_i h(x_i), \qquad h(t) = \begin{cases} \tfrac{1}{2} t^2 & |t| \leq \delta \\ \delta |t| - \tfrac{1}{2}\delta^2 & |t| > \delta. \end{cases} \]

Convex and \(C^1\). This is the standard element-wise robust loss, not the multivariate norm-based "vector Huber" function.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default delta float

Threshold \(\delta \ge 0\) between the quadratic and linear regimes.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If delta is negative.

Notes

Proximal operator. Element-wise separable; per coordinate,

\[ \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v)_i = \begin{cases} \dfrac{v_i}{1+\gamma} & |v_i| \leq \delta(1+\gamma), \\[6pt] v_i - \gamma\,\delta\,\operatorname{sign}(v_i) & |v_i| > \delta(1+\gamma). \end{cases} \]

The branches join continuously at \(|v_i| = \delta(1+\gamma)\). Equivalently, with element-wise soft thresholding \(S\),

\[ \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) = \frac{v + \gamma\, S_{\delta(1+\gamma)}(v)}{1+\gamma}. \]

Verification lowering. prox_huberloss uses the soft-threshold form: a single SoftThreshold step with threshold \(\delta(1+\gamma)\) followed by affine arithmetic.

class HuberLoss(ProxableFunction):
    r"""
    Element-wise Huber loss.

    Represents

    $$
        f(x) = \sum_i h(x_i),
        \qquad
        h(t) = \begin{cases}
            \tfrac{1}{2} t^2                        & |t| \leq \delta \\
            \delta |t| - \tfrac{1}{2}\delta^2        & |t| > \delta.
        \end{cases}
    $$

    Convex and $C^1$. This is the standard element-wise robust loss, *not* the
    multivariate norm-based "vector Huber" function.

    Parameters
    ----------
    delta : float
        Threshold $\delta \ge 0$ between the quadratic and linear regimes.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``delta`` is negative.

    Notes
    -----
    **Proximal operator.** Element-wise separable; per coordinate,

    $$
        \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v)_i = \begin{cases}
            \dfrac{v_i}{1+\gamma}
                & |v_i| \leq \delta(1+\gamma), \\[6pt]
            v_i - \gamma\,\delta\,\operatorname{sign}(v_i)
                & |v_i| > \delta(1+\gamma).
        \end{cases}
    $$

    The branches join continuously at $|v_i| = \delta(1+\gamma)$. Equivalently,
    with element-wise soft thresholding $S$,

    $$
        \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v)
            = \frac{v + \gamma\, S_{\delta(1+\gamma)}(v)}{1+\gamma}.
    $$

    **Verification lowering.** ``prox_huberloss`` uses the soft-threshold form:
    a single ``SoftThreshold`` step with threshold $\delta(1+\gamma)$ followed
    by affine arithmetic.
    """

    def __init__(self, delta: float):
        super().__init__()
        if delta < 0:
            raise ValueError("delta must be non-negative")
        self.delta = delta

    def eval(self, x: np.ndarray) -> float:
        r"""
        Evaluate $f(x) = \sum_i h(x_i)$.

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the function.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            The function value $f(x)$.
        """
        ax = np.abs(x)
        per_coord = np.where(
            ax <= self.delta,
            0.5 * x * x,
            self.delta * ax - 0.5 * self.delta**2,
        )
        return float(np.sum(per_coord))

    def prox(self, arg: np.ndarray, gamma: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Compute $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.

        Uses the closed form, per coordinate,

        $$
            \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})_i = \begin{cases}
                \text{arg}_i / (1+\gamma)
                    & |\text{arg}_i| \leq \delta(1+\gamma) \\
                \text{arg}_i - \gamma\,\delta\,\operatorname{sign}(\text{arg}_i)
                    & |\text{arg}_i| > \delta(1+\gamma).
            \end{cases}
        $$

        Parameters
        ----------
        arg : np.ndarray
            Input point.
        gamma : float, default 1.0
            Step size $\gamma > 0$.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            The proximal point $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.
        """
        theta = self.delta * (1.0 + gamma)
        return np.where(
            np.abs(arg) <= theta,
            arg / (1.0 + gamma),
            arg - gamma * self.delta * np.sign(arg),
        )

    def grad(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Compute the gradient of $f$ at ``x``.

        Per coordinate,

        $$
            \nabla f(x)_i = h'(x_i) = \begin{cases}
                x_i                                     & |x_i| \leq \delta \\
                \delta\,\operatorname{sign}(x_i)         & |x_i| > \delta.
            \end{cases}
        $$

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the gradient.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            The gradient $\nabla f(x)$.
        """
        return np.where(np.abs(x) <= self.delta, x, self.delta * np.sign(x))

docs.text:
Bases: ProxableFunction

Indicator of the affine set \(\{x : Ax = b\}\).

Represents

\[ f(x) = I_{\{Ax = b\}}(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } Ax = b \\ +\infty & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default A ndarray

Constraint matrix of shape (m, n), assumed to have full row rank so that \(AA^\top\) is invertible.

required b float, np.ndarray, or LinearExpression

Right-hand side of shape (m,). A scalar is broadcast; a LinearExpression is treated as a parameter by the verification lowering.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If A is not 2-D, or b does not match the row count of A.

See Also

IndPolyhedral : Inequality-constrained counterpart \(\{Ax \le b\}\).

Notes

Proximal operator. The Euclidean projection onto the affine set, independent of \(\gamma\). Its KKT conditions form the block system

\[ \begin{bmatrix} I_n & A^\top \\ A & 0_{m\times m} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} u \\ \nu \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} v \\ b \end{bmatrix}, \]

whose solution is \(u = v - A^\top (AA^\top)^{-1}(Av - b)\).

Verification lowering. prox_indaffine posts the two KKT rows as linear equalities on fresh iterates \(u\) and \(\nu\); it never forms \((AA^\top)^{-1}\) and needs no complementarity constraints.

class IndAffine(ProxableFunction):
    r"""
    Indicator of the affine set $\{x : Ax = b\}$.

    Represents

    $$
        f(x) = I_{\{Ax = b\}}(x) = \begin{cases}
            0       & \text{if } Ax = b \\
            +\infty & \text{otherwise.}
        \end{cases}
    $$

    Parameters
    ----------
    A : np.ndarray
        Constraint matrix of shape ``(m, n)``, assumed to have full row rank so
        that $AA^\top$ is invertible.
    b : float, np.ndarray, or LinearExpression
        Right-hand side of shape ``(m,)``. A scalar is broadcast; a
        ``LinearExpression`` is treated as a parameter by the verification
        lowering.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``A`` is not 2-D, or ``b`` does not match the row count of ``A``.

    See Also
    --------
    IndPolyhedral : Inequality-constrained counterpart $\{Ax \le b\}$.

    Notes
    -----
    **Proximal operator.** The Euclidean projection onto the affine set,
    independent of $\gamma$. Its KKT conditions form the block system

    $$
        \begin{bmatrix} I_n & A^\top \\ A & 0_{m\times m} \end{bmatrix}
        \begin{bmatrix} u \\ \nu \end{bmatrix}
        =
        \begin{bmatrix} v \\ b \end{bmatrix},
    $$

    whose solution is $u = v - A^\top (AA^\top)^{-1}(Av - b)$.

    **Verification lowering.** ``prox_indaffine`` posts the two KKT rows as
    linear equalities on fresh iterates $u$ and $\nu$; it never forms
    $(AA^\top)^{-1}$ and needs no complementarity constraints.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        A: np.ndarray,
        b: float | np.ndarray | LinearExpression,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        A = np.asarray(A, dtype=float)
        if A.ndim != 2:
            raise ValueError(f"A must be a 2-D matrix; got shape {A.shape}")
        m, n = A.shape
        if isinstance(b, np.ndarray):
            if b.shape != (m,):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"b must have shape ({m},) to match A's row count; got shape {b.shape}"
                )
        elif hasattr(b, "decomposition_dict"):  # LinearExpression
            if b.ndim != m:
                raise ValueError(f"b LinearExpression must have ndim {m}; got ndim {b.ndim}")
        # else: scalar — broadcasts in numpy arithmetic; LE-stacking lifts as a const.
        self.A = A
        self.b = b
        self.m = m
        self.n = n

    def eval(self, x: np.ndarray) -> float:
        r"""
        Evaluate $f(x) = I_{\{Ax = b\}}(x)$.

        Requires numeric ``b``; a ``LinearExpression`` ``b`` is supported only by
        the verification lowering.

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the function.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            ``0.0`` if $Ax = b$ (within floating-point tolerance), ``+inf``
            otherwise.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If ``b`` is a ``LinearExpression``.
        """
        if hasattr(self.b, "decomposition_dict"):
            raise TypeError(
                "IndAffine.eval requires numeric b; got LinearExpression. "
                "Symbolic b is supported only by the verification-side lowering."
            )
        if np.allclose(self.A @ x, self.b):
            return 0.0
        return np.inf

    def prox(self, arg: np.ndarray, gamma: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Project ``arg`` onto the affine set $\{x : Ax = b\}$.

        Solves the $m \times m$ system $AA^\top \nu = A\,\text{arg} - b$ and
        returns $\text{arg} - A^\top \nu$.

        Requires numeric ``b``; a ``LinearExpression`` ``b`` is supported only by
        the verification lowering.

        Parameters
        ----------
        arg : np.ndarray
            Input point.
        gamma : float, default 1.0
            Step size; unused, since the projection is independent of $\gamma$.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            The proximal point $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If ``b`` is a ``LinearExpression``.
        """
        if hasattr(self.b, "decomposition_dict"):
            raise TypeError(
                "IndAffine.prox requires numeric b; got LinearExpression. "
                "Symbolic b is supported only by the verification-side lowering."
            )
        nu = np.linalg.solve(self.A @ self.A.T, self.A @ arg - self.b)
        return arg - self.A.T @ nu

    def grad(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Not defined: indicator functions are not differentiable.

        Raises
        ------
        NotImplementedError
            Always.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError("Indicator functions are not differentiable.")

Represents

\[ f(x) = I_{\{\|x\|_1 \le r\}}(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } \|x\|_1 \le r \\ +\infty & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default r float or LinearExpression

Ball radius \(r \ge 0\), or a dim-1 LinearExpression treated as a parameter by the verification lowering.

required dual_ub float or None

Upper bound on the KKT multipliers used by the verification lowering. None auto-derives a valid bound from the input box.

If r is negative, or a LinearExpression r is not dim-1.

See Also

Notes

Proximal operator. The Euclidean projection onto the ball,

\[ \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) = \arg\min_{u}\ \tfrac{1}{2}\|u - v\|_2^2 \quad\text{s.t.}\quad \|u\|_1 \le r, \]

independent of \(\gamma\).

Verification lowering. prox_indballl1 encodes the KKT system of the lifted problem

\[ \min_{u, t}\ \tfrac{1}{2}\|u - v\|_2^2 \quad\text{s.t.}\quad -t \le u \le t,\ \mathbf{1}^\top t \le r \]

with complementarity constraints, bounding the multipliers by dual_ub.

class IndBallL1(ProxableFunction):
    r"""
    Indicator of the $\ell_1$ ball $\{x : \|x\|_1 \le r\}$.

    Represents

    $$
        f(x) = I_{\{\|x\|_1 \le r\}}(x) = \begin{cases}
            0       & \text{if } \|x\|_1 \le r \\
            +\infty & \text{otherwise.}
        \end{cases}
    $$

    Parameters
    ----------
    r : float or LinearExpression
        Ball radius $r \ge 0$, or a dim-1 ``LinearExpression`` treated as a
        parameter by the verification lowering.
    dual_ub : float or None, default None
        Upper bound on the KKT multipliers used by the verification lowering.
        ``None`` auto-derives a valid bound from the input box.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``r`` is negative, or a ``LinearExpression`` ``r`` is not dim-1.

    See Also
    --------
    IndBallLinf : The $\ell_\infty$ ball.
    NormInf : Its prox is computed from this projection by Moreau decomposition.

    Notes
    -----
    **Proximal operator.** The Euclidean projection onto the ball,

    $$
        \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v)
        = \arg\min_{u}\ \tfrac{1}{2}\|u - v\|_2^2
        \quad\text{s.t.}\quad \|u\|_1 \le r,
    $$

    independent of $\gamma$.

    **Verification lowering.** ``prox_indballl1`` encodes the KKT system of the
    lifted problem

    $$
        \min_{u, t}\ \tfrac{1}{2}\|u - v\|_2^2 \quad\text{s.t.}\quad
        -t \le u \le t,\ \mathbf{1}^\top t \le r
    $$

    with complementarity constraints, bounding the multipliers by ``dual_ub``.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        r: float | LinearExpression,
        dual_ub: float | None = None,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        if hasattr(r, "decomposition_dict"):  # dim-1 LinearExpression parameter
            if r.ndim != 1:
                raise ValueError("r must be a scalar or a dim-1 LinearExpression")
        elif r < 0:
            raise ValueError("r must be non-negative")
        self.r = r
        self.dual_ub = dual_ub

    def prox(self, arg: np.ndarray, gamma: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Project ``arg`` onto the $\ell_1$ ball of radius $r$.

        Solved numerically with CVXPY (Clarabel) as an independent reference; a
        ``LinearExpression`` ``r`` uses its constant value.

        Parameters
        ----------
        arg : np.ndarray
            Input point.
        gamma : float, default 1.0
            Step size; unused, since the projection is independent of $\gamma$.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            The proximal point $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.
        """
        arg = np.asarray(arg, dtype=float)
        # Numeric reference: a parameter ``r`` uses its stored constant value (cf. IndAffine).
        r = float(self.r.const[0]) if hasattr(self.r, "decomposition_dict") else float(self.r)
        u = cp.Variable(arg.shape[0])
        # Pin CLARABEL: deterministic and accurate (~1e-7) across platforms, unlike
        # cvxpy's auto-selected default (OSQP/SCS) which can return ~1e-3 solutions.
        cp.Problem(cp.Minimize(cp.sum_squares(u - arg)), [cp.norm1(u) <= r]).solve(
            solver=cp.CLARABEL
        )
        return np.asarray(u.value, dtype=float)

class IndBallLinf(ProxableFunction):
    r"""
    Indicator of the $\ell_\infty$ ball $\{x : \|x\|_\infty \le r\}$.

    Represents

    $$
        f(x) = I_{\{\|x\|_\infty \leq r\}}(x) = \begin{cases}
            0       & \text{if } \|x\|_\infty \leq r \\
            +\infty & \text{otherwise.}
        \end{cases}
    $$

    Parameters
    ----------
    r : float
        Ball radius $r \ge 0$.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``r`` is negative.

    See Also
    --------
    IndBox : General box $[l, u]$.
    IndBallL1 : The $\ell_1$ ball.

    Notes
    -----
    **Proximal operator.** The Euclidean projection onto the ball, an
    element-wise clip,

    $$
        \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) = \operatorname{clip}(v, -r, r),
    $$

    independent of $\gamma$.

    **Verification lowering.** ``prox_indballlinf`` posts a single
    ``SaturatedLinear`` step clipping to $[-r, r]$.
    """

    def __init__(self, r: float):
        super().__init__()
        if r < 0:
            raise ValueError("r must be non-negative")
        self.r = r

    def eval(self, x: np.ndarray) -> float:
        r"""
        Evaluate $f(x) = I_{\{\|x\|_\infty \leq r\}}(x)$.

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the function.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            ``0.0`` if $\|x\|_\infty \leq r$, ``+inf`` otherwise.
        """
        if np.linalg.norm(x, np.inf) <= self.r:
            return 0.0
        return np.inf

    def prox(self, arg: np.ndarray, gamma: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Project ``arg`` onto the $\ell_\infty$ ball of radius $r$.

        Computes $\operatorname{clip}(\text{arg}, -r, r)$ element-wise.

        Parameters
        ----------
        arg : np.ndarray
            Input point.
        gamma : float, default 1.0
            Step size; unused, since the projection is independent of $\gamma$.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            The proximal point $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.
        """
        return np.clip(arg, -self.r, self.r)

    def grad(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Not defined: indicator functions are not differentiable.

        Raises
        ------
        NotImplementedError
            Always.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError("Indicator functions are not differentiable.")

class IndBox(ProxableFunction):
    r"""
    Indicator of the box $[l, u]$.

    Represents

    $$
        f(x) = I_{[l, u]}(x) = \begin{cases}
            0       & \text{if } l \leq x \leq u \text{ (element-wise)} \\
            +\infty & \text{otherwise.}
        \end{cases}
    $$

    Parameters
    ----------
    l : float, np.ndarray, or LinearExpression
        Lower bound. A scalar is broadcast; a ``LinearExpression`` is treated as
        a parameter by the verification lowering.
    u : float, np.ndarray, or LinearExpression
        Upper bound, with the same conventions as ``l``.

    See Also
    --------
    IndBallLinf : Symmetric box $[-r, r]$.
    IndNonNegative : One-sided box $[0, +\infty)$.

    Notes
    -----
    **Proximal operator.** The Euclidean projection onto the box,

    $$
        \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) = \min(\max(v, l), u)
        \quad \text{(element-wise)},
    $$

    independent of $\gamma$.

    **Verification lowering.** ``prox_indbox`` posts a single
    ``SaturatedLinear`` step clipping to $[l, u]$. ``LinearExpression`` bounds
    enter through their interval bounds during bound propagation.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        l: float | np.ndarray | LinearExpression,
        u: float | np.ndarray | LinearExpression,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.l = l
        self.u = u

    def eval(self, x: np.ndarray) -> float:
        r"""
        Evaluate $f(x) = I_{[l, u]}(x)$.

        Requires numeric ``l`` and ``u``; ``LinearExpression`` bounds are
        supported only by the verification lowering.

        Parameters
        ----------
        x : np.ndarray
            Point at which to evaluate the function.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            ``0.0`` if $l \leq x \leq u$ element-wise, ``+inf`` otherwise.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If ``l`` or ``u`` is a ``LinearExpression``.
        """
        if hasattr(self.l, "decomposition_dict") or hasattr(self.u, "decomposition_dict"):
            raise TypeError(
                "IndBox.eval requires numeric l and u; got LinearExpression. "
                "Symbolic bounds are supported only by the verification-side lowering."
            )
        if np.all((x >= self.l) & (x <= self.u)):
            return 0.0
        return np.inf

    def prox(self, arg: np.ndarray, gamma: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""
        Project ``arg`` onto the box $[l, u]$.

        Computes $\min(\max(\text{arg}, l), u)$ element-wise.

        Requires numeric ``l`` and ``u``; ``LinearExpression`` bounds are
        supported only by the verification lowering.

        Parameters
        ----------
        arg : np.ndarray
            Input point.
        gamma : float, default 1.0
            Step size; unused, since the projection is independent of $\gamma$.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            The proximal point $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If ``l`` or ``u`` is a ``LinearExpression``.
        """
        if hasattr(self.l, "decomposition_dict") or hasattr(self.u, "decomposition_dict"):
            raise TypeError(
                "IndBox.prox requires numeric l and u; got LinearExpression. "
                "Symbolic bounds are supported only by the verification-side lowering."
            )
        return np.minimum(np.maximum(arg, self.l), self.u)

    def grad(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Not defined: indicator functions are not differentiable.

        Raises
        ------
        NotImplementedError
            Always.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError("Indicator functions are not differentiable.")

def prox(self, arg: np.ndarray, gamma: float = 1.0) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""
    Project ``arg`` onto the box $[l, u]$.

    Computes $\min(\max(\text{arg}, l), u)$ element-wise.

    Requires numeric ``l`` and ``u``; ``LinearExpression`` bounds are
    supported only by the verification lowering.

    Parameters
    ----------
    arg : np.ndarray
        Input point.
    gamma : float, default 1.0
        Step size; unused, since the projection is independent of $\gamma$.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        The proximal point $\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(\text{arg})$.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If ``l`` or ``u`` is a ``LinearExpression``.
    """
    if hasattr(self.l, "decomposition_dict") or hasattr(self.u, "decomposition_dict"):
        raise TypeError(
            "IndBox.prox requires numeric l and u; got LinearExpression. "
            "Symbolic bounds are supported only by the verification-side lowering."
        )
    return np.minimum(np.maximum(arg, self.l), self.u)

Bases: ProxableFunction

Indicator of the closed half-space \(\{x : a^\top x \le b\}\).

Represents

\[ f(x) = I_{\{a^\top x \le b\}}(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{if } a^\top x \le b \\ +\infty & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default a ndarray

Nonzero normal vector of shape (n,). (For \(a = 0\) the set would be all of \(\mathbb{R}^n\) or empty, and the projection is undefined.)

required b float

Offset.

required

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a is the zero vector.

See Also

IndPolyhedral : Intersection of several half-spaces \(\{Ax \le b\}\).

Notes

Proximal operator. The Euclidean projection onto the half-space,

\[ \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(v) = v - \frac{\max(0,\, a^\top v - b)}{\|a\|_2^2}\, a, \]

independent of \(\gamma\).

Verification lowering. prox_indhalfspace posts a single scalar Relu step on \((a^\top v - b)/\|a\|_2^2\) and lifts it back along \(a\).
